## Column 2

For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same <term>Lord (ΚΣ)</term> is Lord of all, bestowing his riches upon all who call on him. For "everyone who calls on the name of the <term>Lord (ΚΥ)</term> will be saved."

How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, "<term>Lord (ΚΕ)</term>, who has believed our report?" So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of <term>Christ (ΧΥ)</term>.

But I ask, have they not heard? Indeed they have; for "their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world." But I ask, did Israel not understand? First Moses says, "I will make you jealous of those who are not a nation; with a foolish nation I will make you angry." Then Isaiah is so bold as to say, "I have been found

## Column 3

by those who did not seek me; I have shown myself to those who did not ask for me." But of Israel he says, "All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people."

I ask, then, has <term>God (ΘΣ)</term> rejected his people? By no means! For I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, a member of the tribe of Benjamin. <term>God (ΘΣ)</term> has not rejected his people whom he foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says of Elijah, how he pleads with <term>God (ΘΩ)</term> against Israel? "<term>Lord (ΚΕ)</term>, they have killed your prophets, they have demolished your altars, and I alone am left, and they seek my life." But what is <term>God's</term> reply to him? "I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal."

So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace. But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace. What then? Israel failed to obtain what it sought. The elect obtained it,

So I ask, have they stumbled so as to fall? By no means! But through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, so as to make Israel jealous. Now if their trespass means riches for the world, and if their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their full inclusion mean!

Now some have become arrogant, as though I were not coming to you; but I will come to you quickly, if the <term>Lord <note>original: ΚΣ (Κύριος)</note></term> wills, and I will find out not the talk of those who are arrogant but their power; for the kingdom of <term>God <note>original: ΘΥ (Θεοῦ)</note></term> is not in talk but in power. What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a <term>spirit <note>original: ΠΝΑ (Πνεύματι)</note></term> of gentleness?

## Column 2

For <term>Christ <note>original: ΧΣ (Χριστόϲ)</note></term>, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Therefore let us celebrate the festival, not with the old leaven, the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. 

I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world.

## Column 3

But now I am writing to you not to associate with anyone who bears the name of brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy, or an idolater, reviler, drunkard, or swindler—not even to eat with such a one. For what have I to do with judging outsiders? Is it not those inside the church whom you are to judge? <term>God <note>original: ΘΣ (Θεὸϲ)</note></term> will judge those outside. Purge the evil person from among yourselves. 

Does any one of you, when he has a grievance against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints? Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you incompetent to try trivial cases? Do you not know that we are to judge angels? How much more, then, matters pertaining to this life! 

So if you have such cases, do you appoint as judges those who have no standing in the church? I say this to your shame. Can it be that there is no one among you wise enough to settle a dispute between the brothers? But brother goes to law...

# TO THE CORINTHIANS I

## Column 1

...some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer. No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to humanity; but <term>God (original: ΘΣ)</term> is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also provide the way out, so that you may be able to endure it. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of <term>Christ (original: ΧΥ)</term>? # TO THE CORINTHIANS I

## Column 1

if the hand should say, "I am not of the body," it is not for this reason any less a part of the body. And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," it is not for this reason any less a part of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be? But now <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΣ" (Theos), a "nomen sacrum" or sacred contraction used by early Christian scribes</note> has placed the members, each one of them, in the body just as He desired. If they were all one member, where would the body be? But now there are many members, yet one body. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," or again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you." On the contrary, it is much more the case that the members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary. And those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, upon these we bestow greater honor; and our unpresentable parts have greater modesty, whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But <term>God</term> has composed

<column-break/>

## Column 2

<margin>110</margin> <note>A marginal section number added by a later scribe</note>
the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it, so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another. And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; if a member is honored, all the members rejoice with it. Now you are the body of <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΥ" (Christou)</note> and members individually. And <term>God</term> has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, various kinds of tongues. Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles? Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And I will show you a still more excellent way.

## Column 3

And if I have the gift of prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And if I give away all my possessions, and if I deliver up my body that I may boast, but have not love, I gain nothing. Love is patient, love is kind, love is not jealous, love does not brag, is not arrogant, does not act unbecomingly, does not seek its own, is not provoked, does not take into account a wrong suffered, does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. But if there are prophecies, they will be done away; if there are tongues, they will cease; if there is knowledge, it will be done away. For we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, the partial will be done away. When I was a child,

## Column 1

Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophecy, or by teaching? 
Even lifeless things that give a sound, whether a flute or a harp, if they do not give a distinction in the notes, how will it be known what is being piped or harped? For indeed, if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare himself for battle? 
So also you, unless you give an intelligible word by the tongue, how will it be known what is being spoken? For you will be speaking into the air. 
There are, perhaps, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none is without meaning. If then I do not know the power of the voice, I will be a foreigner <note>original: "barbaros," meaning one who speaks a different language</note> to the speaker, and the speaker will be a foreigner to me. 
So also you, since you are zealots for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound for the 

<column-break/>

## Column 2

edification of the church. 
Therefore, let him who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret. 
For if I pray in a tongue, my <term>Spirit (PNA)</term> <note>Abbreviation for "pneuma"</note> prays, but my mind is unfruitful. 
What is it then? I will pray with the <term>Spirit (PNI)</term>, and I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the <term>Spirit (PNI)</term>, and I will sing also with the mind. 
Otherwise, if you bless <note>correction mark in margin</note> in the <term>Spirit (PNI)</term>, how will he who occupies the place of the uninformed say "Amen" at your giving of thanks, since he does not know what you are saying? 
For you indeed give thanks well, but the other is not edified. 
I thank <term>God (THO)</term> <note>Abbreviation for "Theos"</note> that I speak in tongues more than all of you. But in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I might also instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue. 
<margin>></margin> Brothers, do not be children in your thinking; rather, be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature.

If therefore the whole church comes together in the same place and all speak in tongues, and uninformed people or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds? 
But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or uninformed person enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all; the secrets of his heart become manifest, and so, falling on his face, he will worship <term>God (THO)</term>, declaring that <term>God (THS)</term> is truly among you. 
What is it then, brothers? Whenever you come together, each one <note>the syllable "sy" was added above the line by a corrector</note> has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.

## Column 1

...in another man’s sphere of influence regarding things already prepared.
But "let the one who boasts, boast in the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΩ" (Kyrio). Paul is quoting Jeremiah 9:24.</note>."
For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΣ" (Kyrios)</note> commends.
I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness; but indeed, do bear with me.
For I am jealous for you with a jealousy of <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΥ" (Theou)</note>, for I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΩ" (Christo)</note>.
But I fear that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his craftiness, your thoughts might be corrupted from the simplicity and the purity that is toward <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΝ" (Christon)</note>.
For if the one who comes preaches another <term>Jesus</term> <note>original: "ΙΝ" (Iesoun)</note> whom we did not preach, or if you receive a different <term>Spirit</term> <note>original: "ΠΝΑ" (Pneuma)</note> which you did not receive, or a different gospel which <insert>which</insert> <note>The scribe accidentally wrote the word "which" twice (dittography).</note> you did not accept, you bear with it well enough!
For I consider myself not at all inferior to those "super-apostles."
Even if I am unskilled in speaking, yet I am not so in knowledge; but in every way we have made this evident to you in all things.
Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself...

<column-break/>

## Column 2

...so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΥ" (Theou)</note> to you free of charge?
I robbed other churches by taking wages from them for my ministry to you.
And when I was present with you and was in need, I did not burden anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my need.
And in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will continue to do so.
As the truth of <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΥ" (Christou)</note> is in me, this boasting of mine shall not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I do not love you? <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΣ" (Theos)</note> knows I do!
But what I am doing, I will continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who want an opportunity to be found equal to us in the matter of which they boast.
For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΥ" (Christou)</note>.

It is no great thing, then...

## Column 3

...if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end will be according to their deeds.

What I am saying, I am not saying according to the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΝ" (Kyrion)</note>, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
For you gladly bear with fools, being wise yourselves!
For you bear it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes advantage of you, if someone puts on airs, if someone strikes you in the face.
To my shame I say that we were too weak for that!
But in whatever anyone else dares to boast—I am speaking in foolishness—I also dare.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I.
Are they ministers of <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "ΧΥ" (Christou)</note>?—I am speaking as if I were out of my mind—I am more so: in labors more abundantly, in stripes more exceedingly, in prisons more...

## Column 4

...frequently, in deaths often.
Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day I have spent in the deep.
In journeys often, in dangers from rivers, in dangers from robbers, in dangers from my own people, in dangers from the Gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the wilderness, in dangers at sea, in dangers among false brothers;
in labor and toil, in many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, in many fastings, in cold and nakedness.
Besides these external things, there is my daily pressure: my anxiety for all the churches.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with indignation?
If I must boast, I will boast of the things concerning my weakness.
The <term>God</term> <note>original: "ΘΣ" (Theos)</note> and <term>Father</term> <note>original: "ΠΗΡ" (Pater)</note> of the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "ΚΥ" (Kyriou)</note> <term>Jesus</term> <note>original: "ΙΥ" (Iesou)</note> knows—He who is blessed forever—that I am not lying.

## Column 1

Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Or do you not realize about yourselves that <term>Jesus</term> <note>original: ΙΣ (Ἰησοῦς)</note> <term>Christ</term> <note>original: ΧΣ (Χριστός)</note> is in you?—unless indeed you fail the test! But we pray to <term>God</term> <note>original: ΘΝ (Θεόν)</note> that you may not do anything wrong—not that we may appear to have passed the test, but that you may do what is right, even if we should seem to have failed. For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth. For we rejoice when you <note>The manuscript reads "you" (hymeis), but the context suggests "we" (hēmeis) are weak</note> are weak and you are strong. This is what we pray for: your restoration. For this reason I write these things while I am away, so that when I am present I may not have to be severe in my use of the authority that the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: ΚΣ (Κύριος)</note> has given me for building up and not for tearing down. Finally, brothers, rejoice. Aim for restoration, comfort one another, agree with one another, live in peace; and the <term>God</term> <note>original: ΘΣ (Θεός)</note> of love and peace will be with you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.

for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of <term>Christ (original: Christou)</term>, until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the <term>Son (original: Huiou)</term> of <term>God (original: Theou)</term>, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of <term>Christ (original: Christou)</term>, so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching by the trickery of men, in craftiness toward the scheme of error. # TO THE THESSALONIANS II

## Column 1

Paul and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in <term>God (Θεῷ)</term> our <term>Father (Πατρὶ)</term> and the <term>Lord (Κυρίῳ)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστῷ)</term>: Grace to you and peace from <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term> our <term>Father (Πατρὸς)</term> and the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστοῦ)</term>. We are obligated to give thanks to <term>God (Θεῷ)</term> always concerning you, brothers, just as it is fitting, because your faith is growing abundantly and the love of every single one of you all toward one another is increasing; so that we ourselves boast in you among the churches of <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term> regarding your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions which you endure <note>The scribe added a small "n" (ν) at the end of the line as a correction or standard Greek suffix</note>, a plain indication of the righteous judgment of <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term> so that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term>, for which you are also suffering, since it is righteous in the sight of <term>God (Θεῷ)</term> to repay with affliction those who afflict you, and to give relief to you who are being afflicted, along with us, at the revelation of the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> from heaven with his powerful angels in a flame of fire, giving...

<column-break/>

## Column 2

...vengeance to those who do not know <term>God (Θεὸν)</term> and to those who do not obey the gospel of our <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστοῦ)</term>, who will pay the penalty of eternal destruction away from the presence of the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> and from the glory of his might, when he comes to be glorified among his holy ones and to be marveled at among all those who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed, in that day. Toward which end we also pray always for you, that our <term>God (Θεὸς)</term> may consider you worthy of the calling and may fulfill every desire for goodness and every work of faith in power, so that the name of our <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term> and the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστοῦ)</term>. Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming <note>The Greek term is 'parousia,' often used for the arrival of a king</note> of our <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστοῦ)</term> and our being gathered together to him, that you not be quickly shaken from your composure nor be troubled, neither by <term>Spirit (Πνεύματος)</term> nor by...

<column-break/>

## Column 3

...word nor by a letter as if from us, to the effect that the day of the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> has arrived. Let no one deceive you in any way; for it will not come unless the apostasy <note>A falling away or rebellion</note> comes first and the <term>man (ἄνθρωπος)</term> of lawlessness is revealed, the <term>son (υἱὸς)</term> of destruction, who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called <term>god (Θεὸν)</term> or object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term>, displaying himself that he is <term>God (Θεός)</term>. Do you not remember that while I was still with you I told you these things? And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed in his own time; for the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains now will do so until he is out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the <term>Lord (Κύριος)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦς)</term> will do away with by the <term>breath (Πνεύματι)</term> of his mouth and will bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming, whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and false wonders, and with every deception...

<column-break/>

## Column 4

...of wickedness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. And for this reason <term>God (Θεὸς)</term> sends them a working of delusion so that they believe the lie, in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wickedness. But we are obligated to give thanks to <term>God (Θεῷ)</term> always for you, brothers beloved by the <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term>, because <term>God (Θεὸς)</term> chose you <insert>from the beginning</insert> <note>original: "ΑΠΑΡΧΗϹ" (from the beginning). A later scribe added "ΕΝ" above the ending, possibly suggesting the variant "ἀπαρχήν" (as firstfruits)</note> for salvation in sanctification of the <term>Spirit (Πνεύματος)</term> and faith in the truth, to which he called you through our gospel for the obtaining of the glory of our <term>Lord (Κυρίου)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦ)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστοῦ)</term>. So then, brothers, stand firm, and hold fast the traditions which you were taught whether by word or by our letter. Now may our <term>Lord (Κύριος)</term> <term>Jesus (Ἰησοῦς)</term> <term>Christ (Χριστὸς)</term> himself and <term>God (Θεὸς)</term> our <term>Father (Πατὴρ)</term>, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope by grace, comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.

<summary>This page contains the opening of 2 Thessalonians, where Paul encourages the church through persecution and corrects a misunderstanding that the Day of the Lord had already arrived. He describes a "man of lawlessness" who must be revealed before the final coming of Christ.</summary>

## Column 2

If anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be put to shame; yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.

The <term>Lord (Κύριος)</term> be with you all.

## Column 4

In many parts and in many ways long ago, <term>God (Θεός)</term> spoke to the fathers by the prophets; in these last days, He spoke to us by a <term>Son (Υἱῷ)</term>, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also created the ages.
He is the radiance of His glory and the exact representation of His nature, sustaining all things by the word of His power. After making purification for <note>our <note>The word "our" (ἡμῶν) was added above the line by a later corrector to clarify whose sins were being purified.</note></note> sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, having become so much better than the angels as He has inherited a more excellent name than they.
For to which of the angels did He ever say: You are my <term>Son (Υἱός)</term>, today I have begotten you? And again: I will be to him a <term>Father (Πατέρα)</term> and he shall be to me a <term>Son (Υἱόν)</term>?
And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says: And let all the angels of <term>God (Θεοῦ)</term> worship him.
And regarding the angels He says: He who makes His angels...

<summary>This page contains the theological heart of Hebrews, arguing that Christ's single sacrifice is superior to the repetitive animal sacrifices of the Old Testament. It explains that while the old law was a "shadow," Christ's death establishes a new and final covenant that truly removes sin.</summary>

<summary>This page records the pivotal expansion of the early Church from a Jewish context to a Gentile one, centered in Antioch where the term "Christian" originated. It also depicts the beginning of state persecution under Herod Agrippa I, leading to the martyrdom of James and the miraculous imprisonment and rescue of Peter.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the narrative of Peter’s miraculous escape in Jerusalem (Acts 12) to the beginning of the first missionary journey of Paul and Barnabas. The text here captures a pivotal moment: Saul (now called Paul) confronting a sorcerer on Cyprus, and then delivering a major sermon in a synagogue in Antioch of Pisidia. This sermon is a foundational summary of how the early Church interpreted the history of Israel as leading directly to Jesus.</meta>

<meta>This page continues the narrative of Paul’s legal defense before King Agrippa II and Governor Festus in Caesarea. On the previous page, Festus summarized the case for the King. Now, Paul speaks for himself, recounting his former life as a persecutor of Christians and his miraculous encounter with the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus. The text then transitions into the beginning of Paul’s journey to Rome by sea.</meta>

## Column 1

I tried to force them to blaspheme, and in my raging fury against them, I even persecuted them to foreign cities. On such a journey to Damascus, with the authority and commission of the chief priests, at midday, O King, I saw on the way a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those traveling with me. When we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads." <note>This is a Greek proverb referring to an ox kicking against the sharp stick used by a driver; it suggests struggling against divine will is painful and futile.</note> I said, "Who are you, <term>Lord <note>Nomina Sacra: ΚΕ (Kyrie)</note></term>?" And the <term>Lord <note>Nomina Sacra: ΚΣ (Kyrios)</note></term> said, "I am <term>Jesus <note>Nomina Sacra: ΙΣ (Iēsous)</note></term> whom you are persecuting. But rise and stand on your feet; for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to appoint you as a servant and a witness both of the things you saw and the things in which I will appear to you, delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles—to whom I am now sending you—to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power

of Satan to <term>God <note>Nomina Sacra: ΘΝ (Theon)</note></term>, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me." Having obtained help from <term>God <note>Nomina Sacra: ΘΥ (Theou)</note></term> to this day, I stand here testifying to both small and great, saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen: that the <term>Christ <note>Nomina Sacra: ΧΣ (Christos)</note></term> was to suffer, and that by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles. <meta>This page continues the narrative from the previous chapter, moving from Paul’s legal defense before King Agrippa to the beginning of his hazardous journey to Rome as a prisoner. The text captures the escalating tension of a Mediterranean storm, transitioning from cautious sailing near Crete to a full-scale maritime crisis. The scribe uses paragraphoi (horizontal strokes in the margin) to denote shifts in the action or the start of Paul's speeches.</meta>

<header>THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES</header>

## Column 1

The centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board. After we had sailed slowly for many days and had arrived with difficulty off Cnidus, the wind not allowing us to go further, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone. With difficulty, we coasted along it and came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasaea. Since a considerable time had passed and sailing was now dangerous because even the Fast <note>This refers to the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur), which occurred in the autumn. In the ancient world, this marked the end of the safe sailing season due to the onset of winter storms.</note> had already passed, Paul began to warn them, saying to them: "Men, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives." 
<margin>—</margin>But the centurion was persuaded more by the pilot and the owner of the ship than by what was said by Paul. Because the harbor was not suitable for wintering, the majority reached a decision to set sail from there, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to spend the winter, a

<column-break/>

## Column 2

harbor of Crete looking toward the southwest and the northwest.
<margin>—</margin>When a gentle south wind blew, thinking they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and began to sail close along Crete. But not long afterward, a tempestuous wind called the Euraquilo <note>A "Typhonic" wind, essentially a hurricane-force northeasterly gale common in the Mediterranean.</note> rushed down from the island. When the ship was caught and could not face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along. Running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were scarcely able to get the ship's boat <note>The small skiff or dinghy usually towed behind the main vessel.</note> under control. After hoisting it up, they used supports to undergird the ship; and fearing that they might run aground on the Syrtis <note>The "Syrtis" were notorious and deadly quicksands and shallows off the coast of North Africa.</note>, they lowered the gear and so were driven along. As we were being violently battered by the storm, on the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard, and on the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

<column-break/>

## Column 3

Neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm kept pressing upon us; finally, all hope of our being saved was abandoned. Since they had been without food for a long time, Paul then stood up in their midst and said: "Men, you should have followed my advice not to set sail from Crete and so have avoided this injury and loss. And now I urge you to take courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
<margin>—</margin>For this very night an angel of the <term>God <note>Nomina Sacra: ΘΥ (Theou)</note></term> to whom I belong and whom I serve stood by me, saying: 'Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and behold, <term>God <note>Nomina Sacra: ΘΣ (Theos)</note></term> has granted you all those who are sailing with you.' Therefore, take courage, men; for I believe <term>God <note>Nomina Sacra: ΘΩ (Theō)</note></term> that it will be exactly as I have been told. But we must run aground on some island." 
Now when the fourteenth night had come, as we were being driven across the Adriatic Sea, about the middle of the

<column-break/>

## Column 4

night, the sailors suspected that they were approaching some land. Taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms; and after a short interval, they took soundings again and found fifteen fathoms. Fearing that we might run aground on rocky places, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
<margin>—</margin>As the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea under the pretext of intending to lay out anchors from the bow, Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers: "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved." 
<margin>—</margin>Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall away. Until the day was about to dawn, Paul kept urging them all to take some food, saying: "Today is the fourteenth day that you have been in constant suspense and have continued without eating, having taken nothing."

<summary>This page describes the perilous sea journey of Paul toward Rome, specifically the onset of a violent storm (the Euraquilo) and Paul's prophetic encouragement to the crew during their darkest hour. It highlights the transition from human maritime expertise to divine intervention as the ship faces inevitable destruction.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the transition from the end of the Acts of the Apostles to the beginning of the Letter of James. In the Codex Sinaiticus, the General Epistles (also known as the Catholic Epistles) follow the book of Acts, which differs from the order in many modern Bibles where the letters of Paul come first.</meta>

# THE EPISTLE OF JAMES

## Column 1

James, a servant of <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ), written as a sacred contraction called a 'nomen sacrum'.</note> and of the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note> <term>Jesus</term> <note>original: "Iēsou" (ΙΥ).</note> <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "Christou" (ΧΥ).</note>, to the twelve tribes in the <term>Dispersion</term> <note>The "Diaspora"—Jewish communities living outside the ancestral land of Israel.</note>: Greetings.

Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. And let endurance have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing. 

If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of the giving <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note> who gives to all simply and without reproaching, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, without doubting; for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind. For let that <term>man</term> <note>original: "anthrōpos" (ΑΝΟΣ), here used as a general term for a human being.</note> not suppose that he will receive anything from the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note>—a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways. 

Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation, but the rich man in his humiliation, because like a flower of the grass he will pass away. For the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers—

<column-break/>

## Column 2

—the grass, and its flower falls off, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So also will the rich man fade away in the midst of his pursuits. 

Blessed is the man who endures trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life which he promised to those who love him. Let no one who is being tempted say, "I am being tempted by <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note>"; for <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theos" (ΘΣ).</note> cannot be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one. But each person is tempted by his own desire, being dragged away and enticed. Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is fully grown, brings forth death. 

Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers. Every good act of giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the <term>Father</term> <note>original: "Patros" (ΠΡΣ).</note> of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning. By his own will he gave us birth by the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

<column-break/>

## Column 3

Know this, my beloved brothers: let every <term>man</term> <note>original: "anthrōpos" (ΑΝΟΣ).</note> be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of <term>man</term> <note>original: "anthrōpou" (ΑΝΟΣ).</note> does not produce the righteousness of <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note>. Therefore, putting aside all filthiness and remnant of malice, in meekness receive the implanted word which is able to save your souls. 

But become doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. Because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man observing his natural face <note>literally: "the face of his birth."</note> in a mirror; for he observes himself and goes away and immediately forgets what kind of person he was. 

But the one who looks into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and remains in it—becoming not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work—this man will be blessed in his doing. 

If anyone thinks he is religious while not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, this man’s—

<column-break/>

## Column 4

—religion is useless. Pure and undefiled religion before <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theō" (ΘΩ).</note> and the <term>Father</term> <note>original: "Patri" (ΠΡΙ).</note> is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world. 

My brothers, do not hold the faith of our <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note> <term>Jesus</term> <note>original: "Iēsou" (ΙΥ).</note> <term>Christ</term> <note>original: "Christou" (ΧΥ).</note>, the Lord of glory, with acts of partiality. For if a man with a gold ring and in splendid clothing enters your assembly <note>original: "synagōgēn" (συναγωγὴν), referring to the gathering of the community.</note>, and a poor man in filthy clothing also enters, and you look with favor on the one wearing the splendid clothing and say, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You stand there," or "Sit under my footstool," have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts? 

Listen, my beloved brothers: did not <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theos" (ΘΣ).</note> choose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to those who love him? But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich—

<summary>This page contains the opening of the Epistle of James, emphasizing the importance of enduring trials, the source of temptation, and the necessity of being "doers of the word" rather than just "hearers." It concludes with a warning against showing partiality to the wealthy within the Christian assembly.</summary>
<keywords>James, trials, wisdom, double-minded, crown of life, Father of lights, doers of the word, pure religion, partiality, rich and poor</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Epistle of James, picking up at chapter 2, verse 6. Note that there is a significant gap between the end of the previous page (James 1:11) and the start of this transcription (James 2:6), skipping the discussion on the "perfect law of liberty" and true religion.</meta>

## Column 1

...oppress you and they themselves drag you into courts? Do they not blaspheme the noble name that was invoked over you? If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, "**You shall love your neighbor as yourself,**" you are doing well; but if you show partiality, you are committing sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors. 

For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all of it. For the one who said, "**Do not commit adultery,**" also said, "**Do not murder.**" Now if you do not commit adultery but you do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. 

So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to the one who has not shown mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment. 

What is the benefit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him? If a brother or sister is naked and lacking... 

<column-break/>

## Column 2

...daily food, and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and filled," but you do not give them the necessities of the body, what is the benefit? In the same way, faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself. 

But someone will say, "You have faith and I have works." Show me your faith without the works, and I will show you faith by my works. You believe that <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theos" (ΘΣ), a 'nomen sacrum' or sacred contraction.</note> is one; you do well. Even the demons believe—and they shudder. 

Do you want to know, O foolish <term>man</term> <note>original: "anthrōpe" (ΑΝΕ).</note>, that faith without works is useless? Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up Isaac his <term>son</term> <note>original: "huion" (ΥΝ).</note> upon the altar? You see that faith was working together with his works, and by the works, faith was perfected. And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, "**Abraham believed <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theō" (ΘΩ).</note>, and it was credited to him as righteousness,**" and he was called the friend of <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note>. You see that by works...

<column-break/>

## Column 3

...a person is justified, and not by faith alone. And in the same way, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way? For just as the body without the <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "pneumatos" (ΠΝΣ).</note> is dead, so also faith without works is dead. 

Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment. For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man, able to bridle his whole body as well. 

If we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we guide their whole body as well. Look at the ships also: though they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the pilot directs. In the same way, the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. Look at how small a fire sets ablaze such a great forest!

<column-break/>

## Column 4

And the tongue is a fire, a world of unrighteousness. The tongue is placed among our members as that which stains the whole body and sets on fire the course of our existence, and is itself set on fire by <note>Gehenna: A reference to the Valley of Hinnom, a place of fiery judgment.</note> Gehenna. 

For every species of beasts and birds, of reptiles and sea creatures, is tamed and has been tamed by the <term>human</term> <note>original: "anthrōpinē" (ΑΝΙΝΗ).</note> species; but no human being is able to tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison. 

With it we bless the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "Kyriōn" (ΚΝ).</note> and <term>Father</term> <note>original: "Patera" (ΠΡΑ).</note>, and with it we curse <term>men</term> <note>original: "anthrōpous" (ΑΝΟΥΣ).</note> who have been made in the likeness of <term>God</term> <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note>. From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so. Does a spring pour out from the same opening both sweet and bitter water? Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet. 

Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his works are done...

<summary>This page contains the famous discourse on the necessity of works as the completion of faith, using the examples of Abraham and Rahab. It also introduces the warning against the dangers of the tongue and the difficulty of taming human speech.</summary>
<keywords>faith and works, Abraham, Rahab, the tongue, royal law, partiality, Gehenna, justification</keywords>

## Column 1

...[show by his] **good conduct** <note>original: "kalēs" (καλήσαν); the start of the word is missing.</note> his works in the **gentleness of wisdom**. For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there is **disorder** and every **vile practice**. But the wisdom from above is first **pure**, then **peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, and sincere**. And the **fruit of righteousness** is sown in **peace** by those who make peace. 

Where do **wars** and **fights** among you come from? Do they not come from this—from your **pleasures** that **wage war** in your members? You **desire** and do not have; you **murder** and **covet** and cannot obtain; you **fight** and **war**; and you do not have because you do **not ask**. You ask and do not...

## Column 2

<margin>OR DOES IT SEEM AND</margin> <note>A marginal correction: "AI DOKEI KAI".</note>
...receive, because you **ask wrongly**, so that you may **spend it on your pleasures**. You **adulteresses**! Do you not know that **friendship with the world** is **enmity with <term>God</term>** <note>original: "Theō" (ΘΩ), a 'nomen sacrum' or sacred contraction used for the name of the Divine.</note>? Therefore, whoever wishes to be a **friend of the world** makes himself an **enemy of <term>God</term>** <note>original: "Theou" (ΘΥ).</note>. 

Or do you think that the **Scripture** speaks in vain? **The <term>Spirit</term>** <note>original: "Pneuma" (ΠΝΑ).</note> that He caused to dwell in us **longs jealously**; but He gives **greater grace**. Therefore it says, "**<term>God</term>** <note>original: "Theos" (ΘΣ).</note> **opposes the proud**, but **gives grace to the humble**." 

**Submit** yourselves therefore to **<term>God</term>** <note>original: "Theō" (ΘΩ).</note>. **Resist the devil**, and he will flee from you. **Draw near to <term>God</term>** <note>original: "Theō" (ΘΩ)</note>, and He will draw near to you. **Cleanse your hands**, you sinners, and **purify your hearts**, you double-minded. **Be miserable** and **mourn** and **weep**; let your **laughter** be turned into **mourning** and your **joy** into **gloom**. 

**Humble yourselves** therefore before the **<term>Lord</term>** <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note>, and He will exalt you. Do not **speak evil** of one another, brothers. The one who speaks evil of a brother or **judges** his brother...

<column-break/>

## Column 3

...speaks evil of the **law** and **judges the law**; but if you judge the law, you are not a **doer of the law** but a **judge**. There is **one Lawgiver and Judge**, the one who is able to **save** and to **destroy**; but who are you to judge your **neighbor**? 

Come now, you who say, "**Today or tomorrow we will go to such-and-such a city and spend a year there and trade and make a profit**"—you who do not even know what **tomorrow** will bring. What is your **life**? For you are a **mist** that appears for a little while and then **vanishes**. Instead you ought to say, "If the **<term>Lord</term>** <note>original: "Kyrios" (ΚΣ).</note> **wills**, we will live and do this or that." 

But now you **boast in your arrogance**; all such boasting is **evil**. So for the one who **knows the right thing to do** and does not do it, it is **sin** for him. 

Come now, you **rich**, weep and **howl** for the **miseries** that are coming upon you. Your **riches** have **rotted**, and your **garments** are **moth-eaten**.

<column-break/>

## Column 4

Your **gold** and **silver** have **corroded**, and their **rust** will be a **witness** against you and will **eat your <insert>your</insert>** <note>the word "hymōn" (your) was added by a later scribe between the lines.</note> **flesh like fire**. You have **laid up treasure** in the **last days**. 

Behold, the **wages of the laborers** who mowed your fields, which were **kept back by you**, cry out; and the **cries of the harvesters** have reached the ears of the **<term>Lord of Sabaoth</term>** <note>original: "Kyriou Sabaoth" (ΚΥ σαβαὼθ). 'Sabaoth' is a Hebrew title meaning 'of hosts' or 'of armies'.</note>. You have **lived in luxury** on the earth and in **self-indulgence**; you have **fattened your hearts** as in a **day of slaughter**. You have **condemned**; you have **murdered the righteous one**; he does not resist you. 

**Be patient**, therefore, brothers, until the **coming of the <term>Lord</term>** <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note>. Behold, the **farmer** waits for the **precious fruit** of the earth, being patient over it until it receives the **early and late rain** <note>A marginal note and marker appear here, likely indicating a textual variant or a liturgical reading break regarding the "fruit".</note>. 

You also **be patient**; **strengthen your hearts**, because the **coming of the <term>Lord</term>** <note>original: "Kyriou" (ΚΥ).</note> has **drawn near**. Do not **grumble** against one another, brothers, so that you may not be **judged**; behold, the **Judge** is **standing at the doors**!

## Column 2

**Elijah** was a <term>man</term> <note>original: "ANOS" (anthrōpos). ## Column 3

-> THE FIRST [LETTER] <-

**Peter**, an **apostle** of <term>Jesus Christ</term> <note>original: "IY XY" (Iēsou Christou).</note>, to the **chosen sojourners** of the **Diaspora** <note>This refers to the "dispersion" or scattering of believers across the Roman provinces.</note> in **Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia**, according to the **foreknowledge** of <term>God</term> the <term>Father</term> in the **sanctification** of the <term>Spirit</term> for **obedience** and the **sprinkling of the blood** of <term>Jesus Christ</term>: May **grace** and **peace** be multiplied to you.

**Blessed** be the <term>God</term> and <term>Father</term> of our <term>Lord</term> <term>Jesus Christ</term>! According to his **great mercy**, he has given us **new birth** into a **living hope** through the **resurrection** of <term>Jesus Christ</term> from the dead, into an **inheritance** that is **imperishable, undefiled, and unfading**, kept in **heaven** for you who are being **guarded** by the **power** of <term>God</term> through **faith** for a **salvation** ready to be **revealed** in the **last time**. 

In this you **rejoice**, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been **grieved** by **various trials**, so that the **tested genuineness** of your **faith**—more **precious than gold** that perishes though it is **tested by fire**—may be found to result in **praise and glory and honor** at the **revelation** of <term>Jesus Christ</term>. Though you have not seen him...

<column-break/>

## Column 4

...you **love him**. Though you do **not now see him**, you **believe** in him and **rejoice** with **joy unspeakable** and filled with **glory**, obtaining the **outcome** of your **faith**, the **salvation of your souls**. 

Concerning this **salvation**, the **prophets** who prophesied about the **grace** that was to be yours **searched and inquired** carefully, inquiring what person or time the <term>Spirit</term> of <term>Christ</term> within them was indicating when he **predicted** the **sufferings** of <term>Christ</term> and the **subsequent glories**. It was **revealed** to them that they were **serving** not themselves but **you**, in the things that have now been **announced** to you through those who **preached the good news** to you by the <term>Holy Spirit</term> sent from heaven—things into which **angels long to look**.
